messages.subject: Leaving the R pkg team
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Just to tell you that I am leaving the R pkg team. I haven’t used R for
quite some time now, and I need to unload some packaging
responsibilities in Debian.

I have removed myself from the Uploaders field of the few packages that
were under my direct responsibility.

Also note that I orphaned ess, the Emacs mode for R. I had taken it
over from Dirk two years ago. It’s currently maintained within the
Debian Emacs Team, but feel free to adopt it and move it somewhere else
(possibly even in this team).

Thanks for all the work you do, and see you elsewhere in Debian!

Best wishes,

P.S.: I’m going to unsubscribe from this list, so please CC me if you
reply.

--

messages.subject: Bug#1094338: ITP: r-cran-qgam -- Smooth Additive Quantile Regression Models
messages.subject_clean: Bug#1094338: ITP: r-cran-qgam -- Smooth Additive Quantile Regression Models
messages.body_plain:
Package: wnpp
Severity: wishlist
X-Debbugs-Cc: debian-r at lists.debian.org, crusoe at debian.org

Subject: ITP: r-cran-qgam -- Smooth Additive Quantile Regression Models
Package: wnpp
Owner: Michael R. Crusoe <crusoe at debian.org>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-cran-qgam
  Version         : 1.3.4
  Upstream Author : Matteo Fasiolo,
* URL             : https://cran.r-project.org/package=qgam
* License         : GPL-2+
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : Smooth Additive Quantile Regression Models
 Smooth additive quantile regression models, fitted using the methods of
 Fasiolo et al. (2020) <doi:10.1080/01621459.2020.1725521>. See Fasiolo
 at al. (2021) <doi:10.18637/jss.v100.i09> for an introduction to the
 package. Differently from 'quantreg', the smoothing parameters are
 estimated automatically by marginal loss minimization, while the
 regression coefficients are estimated using either PIRLS or Newton
 algorithm. The learning rate is determined so that the Bayesian credible
 intervals of the estimated effects have approximately the correct
 coverage. The main function is qgam() which is similar to gam() in
 'mgcv', but fits non-parametric quantile regression models.

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-qgam
It is a build-dependency of r-cran-dharma, itself a test dependency for r-cran-glmmtmb

  Description     : Datasets for 'gap'
 Datasets associated with the 'gap' package. Currently,

   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-gap.datasets
It is a build dependency of r-cran-gap, itself a build-dependency of r-cran-dharma

Subject: ITP: r-cran-gap -- Genetic Analysis Package
Package: wnpp
Owner: Michael R. Crusoe <crusoe at debian.org>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-cran-gap
  Version         : 1.6
  Upstream Author : Jing Hua Zhao <jinghuazhao at hotmail.com>,
* URL             : https://cran.r-project.org/package=gap
* License         : GPL-2+
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : Genetic Analysis Package
 As first reported [Zhao, J. H. 2007. "gap: Genetic Analysis Package". J
 Stat Soft 23(8):1-18. <doi:10.18637/jss.v023.i08>], it is designed as an
 integrated package for genetic data analysis of both population and
 family data. Currently, it contains functions for sample size
 calculations of both population-based and family-based designs,
 probability of familial disease aggregation, kinship calculation,
 statistics in linkage analysis, and association analysis involving
 genetic markers including haplotype analysis with or without
 environmental covariates. Over years, the package has been developed in-
 between many projects hence also in line with the name (gap).

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-gap
This package is a build-dependency of r-cran-dharma, itself a test dependency of r-cran-performance

messages.subject_clean: Bug#1094346: ITP: r-cran-dharma -- Residual Diagnostics for Hierarchical (Multi-Level / Mixed)
messages.body_plain:
Package: wnpp
Severity: wishlist
X-Debbugs-Cc: debian-r at lists.debian.org, crusoe at debian.org

Subject: ITP: r-cran-dharma -- Residual Diagnostics for Hierarchical (Multi-Level / Mixed)
Package: wnpp
Owner: Michael R. Crusoe <crusoe at debian.org>
Severity: wishlist

* Package name    : r-cran-dharma
  Version         : 0.4.7
  Upstream Author : Copyright: FIXME-2024 Florian Hartig,
* URL             : https://cran.r-project.org/package=DHARMa
* License         : GPL-3+
  Programming Lang: GNU R
  Description     : Residual Diagnostics for Hierarchical (Multi-Level / Mixed)
       Regression Models The 'DHARMa' package uses a simulation-based
       approach to create readily interpretable scaled (quantile)
       residuals for fitted (generalized) linear mixed models. Currently
       supported are linear and generalized linear (mixed) models from
       'lme4' (classes 'lmerMod', 'glmerMod'), 'glmmTMB', 'GLMMadaptive',
       and 'spaMM'; phylogenetic linear models from 'phylolm' (classes
       'phylolm' and 'phyloglm'); generalized additive models ('gam' from
       'mgcv'); 'glm' (including 'negbin' from 'MASS', but excluding quasi-
       distributions) and 'lm' model classes. Moreover, externally
       created simulations, e.g. posterior predictive simulations from
       Bayesian software such as 'JAGS', 'STAN', or 'BUGS' can be
       processed as well. The resulting residuals are standardized to
       values between 0 and 1 and can be interpreted as intuitively as
       residuals from a linear regression. The package also provides a
       number of plot and test functions for typical model
       misspecification problems, such as over/underdispersion, zero-
       inflation, and residual spatial, phylogenetic and temporal
       autocorrelation.

Remark: This package is maintained by Debian R Packages Maintainers at
   https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-dharma
This package is test-dependency of r-cran-performance
